New: Tiers. Every tracked character now gets an overall letter from S to D, and a letter in each statistics category. Letters compare a character with everyone else on the same ruleset, over their whole career: by default the top 5% get S, the next 15% A, the next 30% B, the next 30% C and the bottom 20% D.

How a letter is worked out: each statistic that counts gives you a percentile (how much of your ruleset you are ahead of, with ties sharing). A category's score is the average of your percentiles in it, and your overall score is the average of your category scores, each category weighing the same. Your letter comes from where that score places on your ruleset.

"Why this tier" on every character page shows everything behind the letters: each category's score, letter and rank, and for every statistic that counts, your value and your percentile. Open a category to see where to improve.

Only statistics that have been reviewed and approved count toward a tier. Deaths and similar "bad" statistics never do, statistics that count the same thing are graded once, and farmable categories (Social; Camping & Hearth) get their own letter but don't count toward the overall letter. The new "How tiers work" page lists exactly what counts in each category, along with the current letter shares and minimums.

Unranked, and why. A ruleset is graded once it has 50 tier-eligible characters (level 10 and up, fully fetched, not hidden); until then everyone on it is Unranked, and the page says how many are tracked so far. A category letter needs a value above zero in at least half of its graded statistics, so one lucky statistic can't earn an S, and an overall letter needs a letter in at least half of the categories that count toward it. Every Unranked badge says which of these applies.
Tier boards: every ruleset's characters ranked by overall score with their letter, plus a board for each category. Find them from the leaderboards page.
Letters show next to characters on guild rosters, search results, your dashboard and public profiles. Guild pages show how the guild's tracked members spread across the letters, Unranked included.

Everyone is graded again every few hours and after the daily refresh. A character you look up is graded straight after its fetch, against the ruleset's most recent full grading; the page says when it was graded.
Improved: Statistics on character pages are full-width sections that start collapsed, so the page no longer has gaps between categories of different lengths. Click a category's header (or press Enter on it) to open or close it; each one's header shows its letter, how many statistics it has and your best rank in it.
Statistics that don't count toward a tier say so: "not graded" for leaderboard-only statistics, "not graded yet" for ones still waiting to be reviewed.
Fixed: Core stats: weapon damage ranges such as "Main hand damage" no longer wrap onto two lines. They show as whole numbers (45–64) in the same right-hand column as every other number; hover for the exact values.

Guild pages say "of 1 guild", not "of 1 guilds", and list a guild board under "On the guild boards" only once at least 3 guilds are ranked on it, because "#1 of 1" says nothing. When no board has enough guilds yet, the page says so.

New: Guild pages. Every guild has its own page at everstats.app/g/guild-name, linked from every guild name on the site: on character pages, public profiles, leaderboards and search. It shows the guild's faction, ruleset and the date it was created in game, how many members are on Blizzard's roster and how many of them Everstats tracks, the guild's totals for Times camped, Total deaths, Quests completed and Creatures killed, and where the guild stands on the guild boards.

The roster lists every tracked member with their level, class, race, guild rank and when they were last seen in game, and can be sorted by any column or filtered by class. Blizzard only gives guild ranks as numbers, so the guild master shows as "Guild Master" and everyone else as "Rank 1", "Rank 2" and so on. Members under level 10, or not fetched yet, are counted but not named.
Top members: every statistic, grouped like the character page, with the guild's own top five and a "See all" board for just that guild. Overall, this week, or the last 29 days.

Guild leaderboards: guild against guild, on every statistic and every ruleset. Guilds are ranked by the total of their members or by the average per member (switch on each board), overall, this week, or over the last 29 days. A guild is ranked once it has at least 5 tracked members; smaller guilds show as "Not ranked yet" with how many more they need. The figures always come from a guild's current members: someone who leaves takes their numbers with them, and their gains this week count for the guild they're in now.
The leaderboards page has a Characters | Guilds switch, keeping your ruleset and the category list.
The Guilds page lets you search for a guild by name and lists the largest guilds on each ruleset by tracked members.
Search finds guilds as well as characters. As you type, it suggests the characters and guilds Everstats knows, each labelled, and anything that isn't a name and surname opens a results page.
Improved: The rolling board is now "Last 29 days" (it was 26). Backups no longer hold any game data from Blizzard, so the site can keep it 29 days and still never hold anything older than Blizzard's 30-day limit.

Backups now contain only Everstats' own data: accounts, usernames, sign-ins, passkeys, two-factor settings, pins, profiles, settings, beta membership and which characters are yours or hidden. Because none of it is Blizzard's, the last 14 nightly backups and the first backup of every month are kept, instead of 3 days. After a restore, game data (statistics, gear, guilds, history) is fetched from Blizzard again, characters as their owners sign in or someone looks them up.
Hidden characters never appear on a guild page and never count toward a guild's totals or its place on a board.
Fixed: Settings now highlights the section you're actually looking at: Profile on first load, and Delete account at the bottom of the page or when you click it. On a phone, the section bar slides to keep the highlighted section in view.
Character pages no longer show off-hand weapon numbers (damage, speed, DPS) when nothing is equipped in the off hand. The same goes for an empty main hand or ranged slot.

releases.title: 30 days of history, fuller profiles, a proper character sheet

New: Profiles say more about you: a short bio, links to your Twitch, YouTube, X, Bluesky, Kick, TikTok, Instagram or Discord server (you type just your handle and Everstats builds the link), when you joined, your main ruleset and faction, your guilds, and your pinned statistics with their ranks. Fill them in under Settings → Profile. Anything you leave empty simply doesn't show, and your pinned statistics can be switched off.
Core stats on the character page are grouped like the in-game character sheet (Base, Health & power, Melee, Ranged, Spell, Defense, Resistances) and laid out side by side across the page.
Improved: Everstats now keeps game data from Blizzard for at most 30 days, as Blizzard's rules for its API require. The site keeps 26 days and its backups 3 more, so nothing is ever older than 30. History, rank movement and progress go back about four weeks and no further.
"Monthly" boards are now "Last 26 days": what each character gained over the most recent 26 days, a rolling window that opens once there are 26 days of snapshots. Weekly boards are unchanged.

If Blizzard stops returning a character (deleted, renamed or made private), its page and your character list say so with the date, and its old numbers come off the boards straight away instead of being shown as current. If it doesn't come back within 30 days, everything Everstats had about it is deleted.
The footer says where character data comes from: Blizzard Entertainment's game data API.
The privacy page explains the 30-day limit.

For the site owner: a Data retention panel on the admin page shows the window, the last sweep, what it deleted and the age of the oldest game data stored. Backups are now kept 3 days each instead of 14 plus one a month, because they hold game data too. Discovery runs older than the window are deleted, and the Discovery page says so.
Fixed: "Choose a username" no longer wraps onto its own row in the top bar at mid-sized widths.
Going to /dashboard now takes you to your dashboard instead of "Nothing here".
The "Claim your username" prompt no longer appears over the admin area.

releases.title: Usernames, profiles, and gear that looks like the game

New: Usernames. Claim yours (first come, first served) and you get a public profile at everstats.app/u/yourname, showing your display name, beta membership, your featured character and your other characters that aren't hidden. Until you claim one you're asked at each sign-in; "Not now" keeps a placeholder that nobody else sees. Your BattleTag and Discord name are never used as your name.
Display names: what people see on your profile and at the top of the page. Change yours any time in Settings; it starts as your username.
One free rename (more may come later). A name you rename away from is kept for you for 30 days, and its profile address points to your new one.
Character pages say who claimed a character ("Claimed by @name"), once its owner has a username and as long as the character isn't hidden.

Gear looks like the game's character sheet: item icons framed in their quality colour around the character, weapons along the bottom, and a tooltip like the in-game one on hover, tap or keyboard focus. It shows everything Blizzard sends for the item, in the game's order: binding, slot and type, damage and speed, armor, stats, enchantments, "Equip:" and "Use:" effects, the set with the pieces you're wearing and its bonuses, durability, requirements and sell price.
Improved: Settings keeps its section list in view as you scroll and marks the section you're reading. On a phone it's a bar pinned under the top bar.
The top bar shows your display name and @username instead of "Account".

For the site owner: the admin page can look players up by username, set how many renames an account has, give a reserved name to a verified partner, take a name back for impersonation or abuse, and edit the reserved-name list. It also warns when TRUSTED_PROXIES doesn't match the server's own network.
Fixed: A statistic at zero no longer shows a rank. "#2 of 116" for zero kills read like an achievement; it now says "Not ranked", and ranks read "#1 of 3 with any", counting only the characters who have actually done it. A board where nobody has any yet says so.
The server's internal network now has a fixed address, so the setting that lets rate limits tell visitors apart can't silently stop working when the network is recreated.

releases.title: The beta: real characters, real leaderboards

New: The beta is open, to everyone. A "Beta" badge sits beside the logo and a slim banner under the top bar (you can dismiss it) leads to a new Beta page: what the beta is, and what beta members get. Every account made while the beta is open is a beta member for good, and Settings shows yours ("Beta member since …"). The Beta Tester badge itself arrives with 1.0.

Character pages are real. Search a name and surname and Everstats fetches the character from Blizzard on the spot: the full-body render, level, race, class, faction, ruleset and guild, when they were last seen in game, their gear and core stats, and every in-game statistic grouped by category. Each statistic shows its value, its rank on that ruleset ("#12 of 340"), and how fresh it is. Statistics that come with a name ("Creature type killed the most: Undead") show the name beside the number. Tiers are the next build, and the page says so instead of showing a grade.

A leaderboard for every statistic on every ruleset, browsable by category, each with its top three at a glance. Ties share a rank, characters at zero share the last one, and a board where everyone has the same value says so instead of inventing an order. Each board shows how many characters are tracked on that ruleset.

Weekly and monthly boards rank what characters gained: the week runs from the US weekly reset (Tuesday 15:00 UTC), the month is the calendar month in UTC. A character's gain counts from its first daily snapshot in that week or month. Until snapshots cover a whole week or month, those boards say "Collecting data" and when they open, rather than show a partial ranking.

Signing in with Battle.net brings in every Forever character on your account at once, marked as yours. Characters under level 10, or not yet visible at Blizzard, are listed with the reason. "No Forever characters" and "we couldn't check" are different answers, and "Refresh my characters" reads the list again. Signed in with Discord only? Link Battle.net in Settings to bring your characters in.

Signed in, the home page is your dashboard: a featured character (your highest level unless you pick one), pinned statistics with their rank and its movement since last week ("—" until a week of history exists), and all your characters. Pin statistics from any character page or with "Choose pins". New accounts start with Times camped, Total deaths, Quests completed and Creatures killed.
Hide any of your characters in Settings: a hidden character has no public page and is on no leaderboard, and you still see it.
Every tracked character is refreshed daily, and keeps a snapshot of its statistics every day, forever. Guild rosters bring their level 10+ members in too.

A Privacy page: what an account stores, where character data comes from, how hiding works, and how to delete your account. Accounts can now be deleted from Settings; characters stay tracked as public data, and hidden ones stay hidden.

For the site owner: the crawler on the admin page shows the queue by priority, requests in the last hour and each UTC hour, characters checked and fetched today, the last error and any back-off, with a request budget, a pause for the background crawl and a switch for roster seeding. The beta opens and closes from the admin page, and its perks list is editable there. New statistics the crawler sees appear on the Discovery page for approval by themselves.
Improved: Visiting /admin without an admin session now goes to the admin sign-in page.

releases.title: Discovery: one catalog to approve from

New: For the site owner: the Discovery page has an "All runs combined" catalog with every statistic from every finished run, and which runs each one came from. A character sampled by more than one run counts once, with its newest values. It also says which rulesets and factions the combined sample covers. This is the catalog to approve suggestions from, and it downloads as CSV.
"Re-analyse all runs" re-analyses every finished run with the current rules and rebuilds the combined catalog, using only the responses already stored. It asks Blizzard nothing.
A statistic's value type can be confirmed or corrected. The new "Guessed types" view lists every type that is still a guess. Your choice replaces the guess and survives later re-analyses.
Fixed: Two statistics with identical values are no longer treated as the same thing. "Professions learned" and "Professions at maximum skill" matched only because the sampled characters were low level. Equal values now produce a "possible duplicate" suggestion that shows its evidence: how many characters have both, and how many of those values are non-zero. It is a "likely" duplicate when the names also say the same thing ("Total deaths" and "Deaths"). A name that adds a qualifier, like "World" or "and other things", doesn't count as the same thing. Nothing stops counting toward a tier as a duplicate until you approve the pairing, and both always keep their leaderboards.

Value types no longer read too much into a name. "Battlegrounds played" was taken for a length of time; it's a count. Time, gold and distance now need the name to state a unit or say so plainly, everything else defaults to a count, and anything that is still a guess says "guessed".

releases.title: Discovery: what the first run taught us

Improved: For the site owner: discovery now records each character's ruleset from its profile, and the Answers tab says how many sampled characters are on each ruleset, since tiers are graded within a ruleset.

Suggestions follow the grading decisions made after the first run. Every statistic gets a leaderboard, ties and name-plus-number ones included. Deaths, mishaps, duels lost and quests abandoned are leaderboard-only. Emotes, times camped and hearthing get their own category tier on the character page but never count toward the overall tier. When two statistics are exact duplicates, both keep a leaderboard and only one is graded.
Suggestions say what each statistic counts toward: its category and the overall tier, its category only, or no tier.

A Re-analyse button rebuilds a finished run's catalog, suggestions and answers with the current rules, from the responses it already stored. It asks Blizzard nothing, and decisions already made still apply.
Fixed: "Average quests completed per day" was taken for a duration; it's now recognised as a rate.
Statistics that come with a name beside their number (like "Creature type killed the most: Undead, 979") are now shown as name + number, ranked by the number.
"Duels lost" is now recognised as a bad statistic.
A discovery run no longer asks for the ruleset index twice: the index's link to itself was being followed as if it were a ruleset.

releases.title: Discovery: finding out what Blizzard's Forever API really returns

New: For the site owner: a Discovery page in the admin area. One button asks Blizzard's WoW Forever API about real characters: a primary character, every Forever character on the owner's Battle.net account, and the primary's guild roster, up to a cap (50 by default). It also asks for the rulesets, the guild's profile, roster, activity and achievements, and every character endpoint that might exist. Every answer is kept exactly as it came back, 404s and failures included, with how long it took and the headers Blizzard sent.

Discovery reads the owner's own characters with a Battle.net authorization asked for on the Discovery page. That token is stored encrypted, only discovery uses it, and it is deleted when Battle.net expires it (about a day). Signing in to Everstats works exactly as before.

Each run builds a catalog of every in-game statistic it saw: Blizzard's id, name and category, a guessed value type, and how many sampled characters have it. The catalog sorts, filters, and downloads as CSV or JSON.

Each statistic comes with three suggestions, each with its reason: which tier category it belongs in, whether it's a "bad" statistic like deaths (leaderboard only, never part of a tier), and whether it's worth a leaderboard at all. The owner approves or rejects them; a rejected one isn't suggested again. Nothing becomes a leaderboard or tier category from this yet.

The run answers the open questions directly: whether statistics exist for Forever's own systems (Camping, Legacy, Housing, Skyborne), how Blizzard addresses names with hyphens, spaces or capitals, whether the account listing is realm-based like retail's, how fresh the data is, whether character renders are available yet, and what rate-limit headers Blizzard sends.
Fixed: The home page said "US realms". Forever has no realms, so it now says "US region". So does the "character not found" message.

releases.title: The new look, and nightly backups

New: Everstats has its own look: "Cartographer's Ledger". A twilight map behind every page, character sheets in a gilt frame, shield-shaped tier badges, and Cinzel lettering for names and headings. Forever, Alliance and Horde are all redrawn; visitors still always see Forever.
The top bar has a character search on every page: type a name and surname (press / to jump to it). On a phone the bar folds into a search button and a menu.
A Guilds link in the top bar. Guild pages aren't built yet, and the page says so.

The database is backed up every night to a separate folder on the server. Each backup is read back in full before it's kept; the last 14 are kept, plus the first of every month for good. If one fails, the earlier ones stay and it tries again an hour later.

For the site owner: the admin page shows how backups are going (the last good one, its size, and why the last one failed if it did) and which addresses Cloudflare's tunnel connects from, to fill in TRUSTED_PROXIES.
Improved: Every page that isn't built yet says so in one clear "Coming soon" panel, and the other empty states stay easy to tell apart: "No data yet" is dashed, "No coverage here" is hatched, and "Unranked" shows the dash shield.

Opening a character now really asks the server and shows a loading sheet while it does, then says plainly that character pages are coming. If the server can't be reached, or you've looked up too many characters too quickly, it says that instead.

Settings: unlinking a sign-in, removing a passkey and turning two-factor off now ask you to confirm first. Recovery codes can be downloaded, copied or printed, and Finish waits until you tick that you've stored them. Choosing a theme confirms it's saved.
The two-factor step at sign-in has a "Use a recovery code instead" switch.
Merging accounts asks you to tick that you understand this account will be deleted before it goes ahead.
Fixed: The sign-in page no longer says sign-in "isn't set up yet" next to the passkey button. Passkeys are always offered. If your browser has no Everstats passkey, it now says: no passkey yet, sign in with Battle.net or Discord, then add one in Settings. "Not configured" is now shown only on a provider whose keys really aren't set.

The server now notes where Cloudflare's visitor-address header comes from on every page load, not only when someone signs in or does something else that's rate-limited, so the right TRUSTED_PROXIES value can be found.

releases.title: The foundations: a site you can open, sign in to, and theme

New: Everstats has a home page with a character search (name and surname). Lookups aren't switched on yet, so a search takes you to the character's page, which says plainly that there's no data for anyone yet.

Every page Everstats 1.0 will have is in place: character pages (hero, gear, core stats, statistics by category, tier letters, progress charts), leaderboards for each ruleset and category, single-statistic leaderboards and guild pages. Each says what it will show and that it's coming, with no sample numbers.

Accounts are optional. Sign in with Battle.net or Discord; the first sign-in makes your account. Until the site's keys are entered, the sign-in page says that sign-in isn't set up yet rather than offering a button that fails.

In Settings you can link a second provider, add passkeys (and then sign in with a passkey), turn on two-factor codes from an authenticator app with ten one-time recovery codes shown once, and merge a second account you made by mistake into the one you keep.

Three themes: Forever (twilight blue and gold), Alliance (royal blue, gold and parchment) and Horde (crimson, charcoal and bronze). Choosing a theme is for signed-in accounts and follows your account to every device; visitors always see Forever.
The version and a link to these notes sit in a bar at the bottom of every page.
